method: Country-authored derived estimates combining newly normalized official structural history with existing Big Count 2006 and FIFA Professional 2023 evidence.
evidence_rules: Federation age and historical event count never directly determine a 1–10 score.
Big Count primarily anchors popularity/access; absolute participation alone does not imply cultural dominance.
Professional 2023 player/club counts inform competition and elite ecosystem depth, not development/support quality by themselves.
Australia preserves governance/league/confederation transitions rather than smoothing across them.
Mexico World Cup hosting is bounded elite-support/infrastructure evidence, not a permanent maximum.
New Zealand post-2010 grants support access/development/support context but are programme evidence, not guaranteed outcomes.

country_notes.ARG: Mature organised and professional football predating 1955, with high but non-maximal access and world-leading competition/tradition bands.
country_notes.MEX: Very large football culture and professional ecosystem; access stays below popularity because Big Count registration/club signals are mixed.
country_notes.AUS: High modern access with lower cultural popularity than football-dominant countries; 1960-63 governance disruption and 2004-06 competition transitions are explicit.
country_notes.NZL: Long institutional tradition and high modern access, but football remains secondary to rugby and absolute competition depth is limited.
